answer: Each participant commits before a future drand quicknet round; only its threshold-BLS pulse then determines the challenge and its parameters. A domain-separated hash binds the pulse to the commitment, so a gale, knoll, or thread label cannot predict a valid task in advance. Commit-reveal verification makes responses auditable, while fresh, unpredictable work denies automated sybil swarms reusable precomputed solutions or offline farming across identities.
